hook: The most famous artist of the 20th century, co-founder of Cubism and painter of Guernica.

pages.x: Pablo Picasso was born in Málaga, Spain, in 1881. His mother said his first word was "piz", short for lápiz, pencil. His father, an art teacher, is said to have given up painting when he saw how well his 13-year-old son drew.
Poor, and grieving for a friend who had taken his own life, from 1901 to 1904 he painted beggars, the blind and the lonely in shades of blue.
In Paris in 1907 he painted five women with faces like African masks, their bodies broken into sharp shapes. Even his friends were shocked. It became one of the founding works of modern art.
With Georges Braque he invented Cubism, showing things from many sides at once, broken into geometric pieces. They also invented collage, gluing paper and newspaper onto their pictures.

pages.t: A suspect for the Mona Lisa
pages.x: When the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre in 1911, the police questioned Picasso, because a friend had once sold him little statues stolen from the museum. He had nothing to do with it.

In 1937, in the Spanish Civil War, German planes bombed the Basque town of Guernica. Picasso painted a huge black and white picture of screaming people and animals. The story goes that a German officer asked him: "Did you do this?" He answered: "No, you did."
He never stopped working: paintings, sculptures, pottery, prints and drawings, some 50,000 works in all. He was often cruel to the women he loved, who were also his models. He died in 1973, aged 91.
Picasso was the most influential artist of the 20th century, and changed what a painting could be.
